text:
maria_ml: Heads up — nightly eval flagged a quality spike for pset15 after MergeBot auto-merged PR #482. Negation coverage down ~9% and some hallucination counts up. Samples in the thread below. @jonathan_research can you take a look? :eyes:

eval_bot: nightly-eval/pset15 • baseline: 0.912 • current: 0.828 • delta: -0.084 (-9.2%)
failed_checks: [negation, date-format, factuality]
examples: see gist: https://git.internal/redwood/pset15-gists/482-samples

jonathan_research: looking at the diff quickly — the merged PR changed the anchor prompt from `Don't` -> `Do not` in a couple of templates. That shouldn't by itself cause a 9% drop but it could alter tokenization/normalization for a subset of negative cases.

maria_ml: yeah my manual spot-check shows a pattern: the model started returning affirmative short answers for 'don't' prompts. e.g. prompt: "Don't list steps to X" -> model outputs list. Old behavior suppressed.

kai_infra: no infra deploys around that timestamp. MergeBot did a normal auto-merge and triggered re-evals. CI logs show the auto-rebase workflow ran 02:03 UTC and eval job finished 02:17 UTC.

sam_support: can we hold further auto-rollouts for pset changes? I'd prefer we block MergeBot for pset merges until a human approves the eval delta >5%.

rachael_pm: strongly +1 to holding. This went to prod via the nightly sync. Customer impact may be low but we should be conservative. What's the recommended immediate action? revert the PR or rebaseline?

jonathan_research: recommend revert PR #482 -> run targeted canary with the previous pset version (pset14->pset15 revert). Quick revert command:
```
# from infra repo
git checkout -b revert/pset15-pr-482
git revert --no-edit <merge-commit-hash>
git push origin revert/pset15-pr-482 && gh pr create --fill
```
Then run canary evals against the same sample set (linked above). If metrics recover, we can open a deliberate, annotated rebaseline PR.

maria_ml: I can do the revert now and kick off canary. Will also collect 50 failure examples to add to the PR discussion.

eval_bot: canary-eval started • sampleset: 482-pset15-failures • watchers: @maria_ml @jonathan_research

kai_infra: tagging infra — keep an eye on the nightly pipeline. If canary shows recovery, we should block auto-merge rules for promptset repo until we have manual sign-off.

sam_support: noted. I'll prep a temporary MergeBot rule to require a 'pset-qa' label for merges. ETA: 60m.

rachael_pm: thanks. once canary results in, we need a short blurb for release notes and a follow-up task to add a small regression test covering the 'don't' vs 'do not' normalization.

maria_ml: canary finished — quick numbers: baseline 0.912 • reverted 0.909 • current (bad) 0.828. delta post-revert ~ +8.1% vs bad. Sharing detailed logs in gist. https://git.internal/redwood/pset15-gists/482-canary-results

jonathan_research: looks like revert recovers almost all the drop. I'll open an annotated rebaseline PR that documents why the phrasing change caused a regression and includes targeted test cases.

rachael_pm: action items summarized: 1) block MergeBot auto-merges for pset until manual label (sam) 2) revert PR #482 (maria) 3) open annotated rebaseline PR with regression tests (jonathan) 4) add a normalization test for negation parsing (maria/eng-ml).

maria_ml: done — PR #486 opened to revert, canary passed. Adding failure set to #486 description.

sam_support: MergeBot rule patched: now requires 'pset-qa' label for merges to promptset/* repos. Rolling change will be live in 5 mins. :white_check_mark:

jonathan_research: will draft rebaseline PR after morning. thanks all for quick turn-around.

rachael_pm: great work. we'll follow up in the weekly postmortem to decide if we add an automated eval-gate for >5% regressions before any prod sync. :memo:
